what_is_checked: reset-fresh / reset-after-partial / reset-after-error / reset-double: the engine reset runs with directive 1 and the whole 24-byte inBuffer (src/size/pos) reads back as zero afterwards; the engine return is 0; a reset after an error (which already reset) and a second reset are both still ok

compress-single-shot: *output_len is 0 first; empty input returns 0 with no engine call; a non-empty input returns 0 (frame complete) with a frame whose descriptor carries the checksum bit and which the independent direct decompress returns to the exact input

compress-resume: with a 16-byte output buffer the first call returns > 0 (bytes still to flush) and resuming with the SAME token completes the same frame byte-for-byte (equal to the independent single-shot frame)

compress-new-token: switching tokens mid-frame does NOT feed the new bytes into the open frame -- the engine ignores them while the frame flushes (verified: the finished frame holds the consumed prefix of A plus only the bytes of B consumed during the flush, usually none) -- and the pending remainder of B starts a NEW frame on the next call, which round-trips to exactly that remainder
compress-forced-error: a simulated engine error returns -1 with *output_len 0 and the inBuffer zeroed (the Reset ran); the event trace shows the error then the reset
uncompress-round-trip: *output_len is 0 first; empty input returns 0; a frame returns 0 with the exact input and *output_len equal to the input length

uncompress-null-resume: with a 64-byte output buffer the first call leaves input remaining (ret > 0); resuming with a NULL input drains the stored buffer across calls; the concatenated output is the exact input and the frame-completion latch is observed
uncompress-corrupt: a bit-flipped frame returns -1 with *output_len 0 and the inBuffer zeroed (the Reset ran)

uncompress-partial: a split feed (prefix drained with NULL resumes, then the rest under a new token) reconstructs the exact input; the return after the prefix call equals (inBuffer.size - inBuffer.pos) read back from the holder memory (the binary's return rule); the frame completes only after the rest is fed

observations: The two Create factories are NOT reconstructed here: 0x61c1c10 is fully reconstructed in merged RE-001-zstd-compress-cache-115 and 0x61c1ce0 in merged RE-001-zstd-decompress-cache-115 (PR #3635). The scope was narrowed from six functions to four when that coverage was found during duplicate-checking; the factory bodies, the options template values and the landing-pad tails are cited from those packets, not re-claimed.

Mid-frame input switch (Compress): switching the input pointer while a frame is still flushing does NOT feed the new bytes into the open frame -- verified live against the system engine: the finished frame holds the consumed prefix of A plus only the bytes of B consumed during the flush (0 in every tested case), and the pending remainder of B starts a NEW frame on the next call, which round-trips to exactly that remainder. The caller contract is therefore: keep passing the same input pointer until Compress returns 0, then switch.

Raw-block consumption (Uncompress): for incompressible (raw) blocks the engine consumes the whole supplied prefix at once and buffers the decoded output internally, so the return (input remaining) can be 0 while output is still pending; for compressed blocks the return tracks decoding progress and stays > 0 until the output buffer drains. Both follow the same binary rule (inBuffer.size - inBuffer.pos).

Frame-completion latch (Uncompress): ZSTD_decompressStream returns 0 only on the call that finishes the frame; later no-op calls report a nonzero hint (9, waiting for the next frame). Completion is therefore a latched event, not a stable return value -- the model latches it.

The isError threshold is STRICTLY greater than (size_t)-120: the callee body is `xor eax,eax; cmp $0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFF88,%rdi; seta %al; ret`. Code 2^64-120 is NOT an error; 2^64-119 is. (An earlier draft of the case ledger used >= and was corrected from the disassembly.)

Create applies only the checksum flag (ZSTD_CCtx_setParameter(cctx, 201, 1)) to the fresh CCtx; the copied options.level is not passed to any setParameter call in the factory, so the CCtx runs at its default level (3) unless some other path sets it. The 48-byte options copy in the compress holder is stored but never read by any of these four methods (nor by the destructors).

The Writer's 48-byte options template (observed in the refresh caller 0x5f041d0): first qword from the global at 0x459aa0 (0x7ffffffffff2; as int32s (-14, INT_MAX), where -14 matches RocksDB's documented default window_bits), 0x100000000 at +0x10, flag byte 1 at +0x28 -- as recorded in the merged compress-cache packet; the full field layout of CompressionOptions is not pinned here.

The shared landing-pad tails sit in the gaps between the functions with their own FDEs: 0x61c1bee..0x61c1c03 deletes the 0x70-byte holder (compress factory's `new` cleanup) and 0x61c1cc8..0x61c1cdd deletes the 0x38-byte holder (uncompress factory's). Neither belongs to Compress/Uncompress themselves.
Reset has no stack canary (no stack array); Compress and Uncompress both build the out struct on the stack and check the canary in the epilogue (__stack_chk_fail at 0x61c1be9 / 0x61c1b29).

The vtable packets list Reset at slot 3 in both tables, but the slot-3 entries' unwind starts (0x101da88 / 0x101daa4) are the FDE-relative offsets, not the Reset FDEs themselves (0x61c1a20 / 0x61c1a50); the body hashes in slots.tsv match this packet's functions.tsv exactly.
